title: Grateful Dead Live at Worcester Polytechnic Institute on 1970-05-09
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy, hissy audience recording of a short acoustic set with standout Jerry performances despite poor sound quality
ai_review.review: The tape captures an intimate early‑1970 acoustic segment that many fans cherish for Jerry Garcia’s folk‑style guitar and harmonica work, as well as rare song moments like "Monkey" and "Black Peter."  Technically the recording is far from pristine – listeners report saturation, hiss and overload, especially on the later electric portion – so the audio quality is judged poor.  Overall sentiment is mixed: the performance earns praise while the sound limits enjoyment.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers commend the acoustic performance (especially Jerry) but repeatedly criticize the recording as muddy, hissy and overloaded; the averaged star score (~2.9) weighted toward show quality yields a modest overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Saturated, hissy and muddy sound; noticeable overload on electric songs, short duration, occasional clipping. Reviewers describe it as more like a microphone‑room capture than a true soundboard feed.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief, acoustic‑focused first set (Jerry and Bob opening) followed by a long break; the electric second half is described as loud but poorly captured. The concert feels intimate yet uneven due to the recording issues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for clear folk‑style guitar, strong vocals and memorable harmonica work; one reviewer notes a slightly tired feel, but most highlight his purity on this tape.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned as part of the acoustic opening with Jerry; no specific performance critique beyond that.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ (likely Pigpen) briefly joins near "Black Peter"; otherwise no detailed keyboard commentary.
